board_events.caption: Rate versus light intensity: the steep climb, then the plateau

board_events.text: External factors: light (intensity, quality, duration), CO2 concentration, temperature, water.
Internal factors: amount of chlorophyll; number, age and orientation of leaves; mesophyll cells.
Light intensity: the rate rises with light, then plateaus — beyond a point another factor (e.g. CO2) becomes limiting, so more light does not help.
CO2 concentration is usually the major limiting factor in nature; raising it (up to a point) boosts the rate. Water acts indirectly — stress closes stomata, cutting CO2 supply.
Temperature strongly affects the enzyme-driven (dark) reactions; C4 plants tolerate and prefer higher temperatures. Assumption: one factor limits at a time — raise it and another soon takes over.

segments.text: No matter how good the machinery, photosynthesis runs only as fast as its scarcest input allows. That single sentence is Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors, and it closes the chapter.

State it properly: when a process depends on several factors, its rate is set by the factor that is nearest its minimum value. That factor is the limiting factor. Raise it and the rate climbs — until something else becomes the bottleneck.
Look at the graph, because the shape is the argument. Steep climb, then a flat plateau. Two regions, two different stories.

First, the list of factors, split into two groups. External: light — its intensity, quality and duration — carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, and water. Internal: the amount of chlorophyll; the number, age and orientation of leaves; and the mesophyll cells themselves.

Now read the light curve. In the steep region, light is limiting: give the plant more light and it photosynthesises faster, because light is the scarcest input. Then the curve plateaus — and beyond that point more light does nothing at all, because light is no longer the bottleneck. Something else, typically carbon dioxide, now limits.

That is why the second, higher curve exists in the figure. Raise the carbon dioxide and the ceiling rises too — proving the plateau was never about light at all. Carbon dioxide is usually the major limiting factor in nature, and raising it, up to a point, boosts the rate.

Water is the subtle one. It acts indirectly, mostly through stomata: under water stress the stomata close, cutting the carbon dioxide supply, and the rate falls. So a water-stressed plant is really a carbon-dioxide-starved plant — which is exactly where photorespiration came from earlier in this subtopic.

Temperature affects the enzyme-driven dark reactions strongly, and C four plants both tolerate and prefer higher temperatures. And note the assumption underneath the law: one factor limits at a time — raise it, and another soon takes over as the new bottleneck. Picture a thali assembly line moving at the speed of whichever dish is in shortest supply. During the monsoon, dim cloudy skies make light the limiting factor, lowering rice yields in eastern India — the law in action, in a field.
Machinery कितनी भी बढ़िया हो, photosynthesis उतनी ही तेज़ चलेगी जितनी उसका सबसे कम input इजाज़त दे। यही एक वाक्य Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors है, और यही chapter बंद करता है।

इसे ठीक से बोलो: जब कोई process कई factors पर निर्भर हो, तो उसकी rate वो factor तय करता है जो अपनी न्यूनतम क़ीमत के सबसे क़रीब है। वही limiting factor है। उसे बढ़ाओ तो rate चढ़ती है — जब तक कोई और चीज़ bottleneck न बन जाए।
Graph देखो, क्योंकि उसका shape ही पूरी दलील है। तीखी चढ़ाई, फिर सपाट plateau। दो इलाक़े, दो अलग कहानियाँ।

पहले factors की list, दो हिस्सों में। External: light — उसकी intensity, quality और duration — carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, और water। Internal: chlorophyll की मात्रा; leaves की संख्या, उम्र और orientation; और ख़ुद mesophyll cells।

अब light curve पढ़ो। तीखे हिस्से में light limiting है: plant को और light दो तो वो तेज़ photosynthesis करेगा, क्योंकि light ही सबसे कम input है। फिर curve plateau हो जाती है — और उस point के आगे और light कुछ नहीं करती, क्योंकि अब light bottleneck है ही नहीं। अब कोई और चीज़, आम तौर पर carbon dioxide, limit कर रही है।

इसीलिए figure में दूसरी, ऊँची curve है। Carbon dioxide बढ़ाओ तो छत भी ऊपर उठ जाती है — साबित हुआ कि plateau light की वजह से थी ही नहीं। क़ुदरत में आम तौर पर carbon dioxide ही मुख्य limiting factor है, और उसे एक हद तक बढ़ाना rate बढ़ा देता है।

Water सबसे सूक्ष्म वाला है। ये indirectly काम करता है, ज़्यादातर stomata के ज़रिए: water stress में stomata बंद हो जाते हैं, carbon dioxide की supply कट जाती है, और rate गिर जाती है। यानी पानी की कमी वाला plant असल में carbon dioxide की कमी वाला plant है — और photorespiration इसी जगह से तो आई थी।

Temperature enzyme-driven dark reactions पर तगड़ा असर डालता है, और C four plants ऊँचा temperature सहते भी हैं और पसंद भी करते हैं। और law के नीचे की assumption नोट करो: एक वक़्त में एक ही factor limit करता है — उसे बढ़ाओ, तो जल्द ही कोई दूसरा नया bottleneck बन जाता है। एक thali line सोचो जो उसी रफ़्तार से चलती है जिस dish की सबसे कम supply हो। Monsoon में धुँधले बादल light को limiting factor बना देते हैं, और पूर्वी भारत में rice की पैदावार गिर जाती है — क़ानून, खेत में काम करता हुआ।

board_events.text: (a) Acceptor: C3 uses RuBP (5C); C4 uses PEP (3C).
(b) First stable product: C3 forms 3-PGA (3C); C4 forms OAA (4C).
(c) Kranz anatomy: absent in C3; present in C4.
Concluding line: because C4 plants concentrate CO2 in their Kranz bundle-sheath cells, they largely escape photorespiration and achieve higher productivity.
Example 2 [NEET Speed Trap]: photorespiration is 'wasteful' because?
Options: (a) it produces excess sugar (b) it synthesises ATP rapidly (c) it produces no sugar, ATP or NADPH while consuming O2 and releasing CO2 (d) it occurs only in the dark.
Answer: (c). (a) inverts reality; (b) confuses it with normal respiration's ATP yield — photorespiration yields none; (d) is wrong because it is light-dependent.

segments.text: Two examples. The first is a board question where the marks live in structure and in one closing sentence. The second is a definition trap dressed up as an explanation question.

Example one, C B S E: give any three differences between C three and C four plants with respect to the acceptor, the first stable product, and Kranz anatomy. The question has handed you the three bases — so answer on exactly those, in exactly that order.
Basis (a), the acceptor. C three uses R u B P, a five-carbon sugar. C four uses P E P, a three-carbon molecule. State both halves; a difference question needs both sides or it is not a difference.

Basis (b), the first stable product. C three forms three P G A, three carbons, hence the name C three. C four forms O A A, four carbons, hence C four. Adding the 'hence' shows the examiner you know why the names exist.
Basis (c), Kranz anatomy. Absent in C three; present in C four. One line, and it is worth the same mark as the harder two.

Now the move that separates a good answer from a full one — the concluding line. Because C four plants concentrate carbon dioxide in their Kranz bundle-sheath cells, they largely escape photorespiration and achieve higher productivity. That sentence ties the three differences into one biological reason, and it is what a board examiner is looking for.
Example two, a N E E T speed trap. Photorespiration is described as wasteful because — and read the options carefully, because two of them are designed for students who half-remember respiration.

The whole point of photorespiration is that it gives nothing useful back. No sugar, no A T P, no N A D P H — yet it consumes oxygen and releases carbon dioxide, undoing carbon that was already fixed. So the answer is (c).

And dissect the traps. Option (a), excess sugar, simply inverts reality. Option (b), synthesises A T P rapidly, is the trap for students who confuse it with normal respiration's A T P yield — photorespiration yields none at all. And option (d), occurs only in the dark, is wrong because photorespiration is light-dependent; the 'photo' in the name is not decoration.
दो examples। पहला board सवाल है, जहाँ marks structure में और एक closing sentence में रहते हैं। दूसरा definition trap है, explanation वाले सवाल के भेस में।

Example one, C B S E: C three और C four plants में कोई तीन फ़र्क़ बताओ — acceptor, first stable product, और Kranz anatomy के आधार पर। सवाल ने तीनों basis ख़ुद दे दिए हैं — तो ठीक उन्हीं पर, ठीक उसी order में जवाब दो।

Basis (a) — acceptor। C three में R u B P, पाँच carbon वाला sugar। C four में P E P, तीन carbon वाला molecule। दोनों हिस्से लिखो; difference वाले सवाल में दोनों पक्ष चाहिए, वरना वो difference है ही नहीं।

Basis (b) — first stable product। C three बनाता है three P G A, तीन carbon, इसीलिए नाम C three। C four बनाता है O A A, चार carbon, इसीलिए C four। ये 'इसीलिए' जोड़ना examiner को दिखाता है कि तुम्हें नामों की वजह पता है।
Basis (c) — Kranz anatomy। C three में absent; C four में present। एक line, और उतने ही mark की जितने बाक़ी दो मुश्किल वाले।

अब वो चाल जो अच्छे जवाब को पूरा जवाब बनाती है — concluding line। चूँकि C four plants अपनी Kranz bundle-sheath cells में carbon dioxide गाढ़ी कर लेते हैं, वो photorespiration से काफ़ी हद तक बच जाते हैं और ज़्यादा productivity हासिल करते हैं। यही वाक्य तीनों differences को एक biological वजह में बाँध देता है, और board examiner यही ढूँढ रहा होता है।
Example two, N E E T speed trap। Photorespiration को wasteful क्यों कहते हैं — और options ध्यान से पढ़ो, क्योंकि इनमें से दो ख़ास उन students के लिए बने हैं जिन्हें respiration आधा-अधूरा याद है।

Photorespiration का पूरा point यही है कि वो बदले में कुछ काम का नहीं देती। न sugar, न A T P, न N A D P H — फिर भी oxygen खाती है और carbon dioxide छोड़ती है, पहले से fix किया हुआ carbon बर्बाद करते हुए। तो answer है (c)।

और traps की चीरफाड़ करो। Option (a), excess sugar, हक़ीक़त को उलट देता है। Option (b), तेज़ी से A T P बनाना, उन students के लिए trap है जो इसे normal respiration की A T P yield से मिला देते हैं — photorespiration ज़रा भी A T P नहीं देती। और option (d), सिर्फ़ अँधेरे में होना, ग़लत है क्योंकि photorespiration light-dependent है; नाम में लगा 'photo' सजावट नहीं है।

board_events.text: Answer: (a) both true, and R correctly explains A. C3 plants close stomata, CO2 falls, O2 rises, RuBisCO turns oxygenase and wastes carbon. C4 sidesteps this entirely.

segments.text: The last two examples, and they are the two the syllabus almost guarantees: a which-goes-where recall, and the assertion-reason that ties the entire subtopic together.
Example three, from C U E T. In C four plants, the primary carbon-dioxide-fixing enzyme and the cell type in which it acts are, respectively — which pair? Answer it before reading the options.

The options: RuBisCO and bundle sheath; P E P carboxylase and mesophyll; RuBisCO and mesophyll; P E P carboxylase and bundle sheath. Notice the design — the paper has taken two enzymes and two cells and offered you all four combinations. Only one is right, and the other three are simply scrambled.

The answer is (b). Initial fixation in C four is by P E P carboxylase, in the mesophyll cells. Read the word 'primary' in the question — it is doing real work, because it is asking which enzyme acts first.

And that is why options (a) and (c) are wrong in an interesting way. RuBisCO does act in C four plants — that is true, and students who know it feel clever choosing it. But RuBisCO acts later, in the bundle sheath, on the released burst. Option (d) simply puts PEPcase in the wrong cell.

Example four, high-difficulty assertion-reason. Assertion: under hot, bright, dry conditions, C four plants outperform C three plants. Reason: C four plants concentrate carbon dioxide around RuBisCO in the bundle sheath, suppressing photorespiration.
Both statements are true — you have met both. So the whole item reduces to one judgement: does the reason explain the assertion, or is it a separate true fact?

Follow the two chains in the figure. Same weather, same closed stomata, two completely different endings. In the C three plant, closing the stomata drops carbon dioxide, raises oxygen, and RuBisCO's oxygenase activity takes over — photorespiration wastes carbon exactly when the plant can least afford it. In the C four plant, PEPcase grabs carbon dioxide even at low concentration and pumps it into the bundle sheath, keeping RuBisCO saturated.

So the reason is not sitting beside the assertion — it is the entire mechanism behind it. The answer is (a): both true, and R correctly explains A. C four plants keep photosynthesising efficiently exactly when C three plants falter, and the carbon dioxide pump is why.
आख़िरी दो examples, और syllabus इन दोनों की क़रीब-क़रीब गारंटी देता है: एक 'कौन कहाँ' वाला recall, और वो assertion-reason जो पूरे subtopic को एक साथ बाँध देता है।
Example three, C U E T से। C four plants में primary carbon dioxide-fixing enzyme और वो cell जिसमें वो काम करता है, क्रमशः — कौन-सी जोड़ी? Options पढ़ने से पहले जवाब दे दो।

Options: RuBisCO और bundle sheath; P E P carboxylase और mesophyll; RuBisCO और mesophyll; P E P carboxylase और bundle sheath। Design देखो — paper ने दो enzymes और दो cells लेकर चारों combinations परोस दिए हैं। सही सिर्फ़ एक है, बाक़ी तीन बस उलटे-पुलटे।

Answer है (b)। C four में शुरुआती fixation P E P carboxylase करता है, mesophyll cells में। सवाल में 'primary' शब्द पढ़ो — वो असली काम कर रहा है, क्योंकि वो पूछ रहा है कि पहले कौन-सा enzyme काम करता है।

और इसीलिए options (a) और (c) दिलचस्प तरीक़े से ग़लत हैं। RuBisCO C four plants में काम करता ज़रूर है — ये सच है, और जिन students को ये पता है वो इसे चुनते वक़्त ख़ुद को होशियार समझते हैं। मगर RuBisCO बाद में काम करता है, bundle sheath में, छोड़े गए burst पर। Option (d) तो बस PEPcase को ग़लत cell में बिठा देता है।

Example four, high-difficulty assertion-reason। Assertion: गर्म, चमकीली, सूखी हालत में C four plants, C three plants से बेहतर करते हैं। Reason: C four plants bundle sheath में RuBisCO के चारों तरफ़ carbon dioxide गाढ़ी कर लेते हैं, जिससे photorespiration दब जाती है।
दोनों statements सही हैं — दोनों से तुम मिल चुके हो। तो पूरा सवाल सिमटकर एक फ़ैसले पर आ जाता है: क्या reason assertion को explain करता है, या वो एक अलग सच्चा fact है?

Figure की दोनों chains के साथ चलो। वही मौसम, वही बंद stomata, और दो बिलकुल अलग अंजाम। C three plant में stomata बंद होते ही carbon dioxide गिरती है, oxygen चढ़ती है, और RuBisCO की oxygenase activity हावी हो जाती है — photorespiration ठीक तभी carbon बर्बाद करती है जब plant उसे सबसे कम बर्दाश्त कर सकता है। C four plant में PEPcase कम concentration पर भी carbon dioxide पकड़ लेता है और उसे bundle sheath में pump कर देता है, RuBisCO को संतृप्त रखते हुए।

यानी reason assertion के बग़ल में खड़ा नहीं है — वो उसके पीछे का पूरा mechanism है। Answer है (a): दोनों true, और R assertion को सही explain करता है। C four plants ठीक तब कुशलता से photosynthesis करते रहते हैं जब C three plants लड़खड़ाते हैं, और वजह है वो carbon dioxide pump।

sections.subtopic: C4 Pathway, Photorespiration & Factors Affecting Photosynthesis
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: the CO2 pre-paid pump, and the slowest dish

board_events.text: Common student pitfalls
Pitfall 1: mixing up the C3 and C4 numbers. C3 → acceptor RuBP (5C), product 3-PGA (3C). C4 → acceptor PEP (3C), product OAA (4C). The naming refers to the first PRODUCT's carbon count.
Pitfall 2: calling photorespiration 'respiration in light'. It is not normal respiration — it makes no ATP. It is RuBisCO's oxygenase blunder, costing the plant carbon.
Pitfall 3: forgetting which enzyme and cell does what in C4. PEPcase → mesophyll (first capture). RuBisCO → bundle sheath (Calvin cycle). Reversing these is a classic error.
Pitfall 4: thinking C4 plants don't use the Calvin cycle. They do — RuBisCO and the Calvin cycle still operate, just safely tucked inside the bundle sheath at high CO2.
Pro-tips
Remember C4 as a 'CO2 pre-paid pump': mesophyll PEPcase loads CO2 into a 4-carbon acid; the bundle sheath unloads it as a concentrated burst for RuBisCO.
For limiting factors, picture a thali line moving at the speed of the slowest dish: raising any other ingredient will not speed things up until you fix the slow one.
Mnemonics: 'PEP loads, RuBisCO reaps'. '4 = OAA, 3 = PGA'. 'Photorespiration = O2 in, CO2 out, nothing gained'. 'Slowest dish sets the thali speed'.

segments.text: This subtopic is among the most heavily tested parts of the chapter, and four pitfalls account for nearly every lost mark. Then two pictures — a pump and a thali line — carry the whole thing into the exam hall.

Pitfall one: mixing up the C three and C four numbers. Fix them as pairs. C three: acceptor R u B P, five carbons; product three P G A, three carbons. C four: acceptor P E P, three carbons; product O A A, four carbons. And the rule that stops the confusion: the naming refers to the first product's carbon count, not the acceptor's.

Pitfall two: calling photorespiration 'respiration in light'. It is not normal respiration. Normal respiration makes A T P; photorespiration makes none. It is RuBisCO's oxygenase blunder, and it costs the plant carbon rather than earning it any.

Pitfall three: forgetting which enzyme and which cell does what in C four. PEPcase, mesophyll, first capture. RuBisCO, bundle sheath, Calvin cycle. Reversing these is a classic error, and the paper will always offer you the reversal as an option.

Pitfall four is subtler and catches good students: thinking C four plants do not use the Calvin cycle. They absolutely do. RuBisCO and the Calvin cycle still operate — just safely tucked inside the bundle sheath at high carbon dioxide. C four is not an alternative to Calvin; it is a delivery service for Calvin.

Now the first pro-tip. Remember C four as a carbon dioxide pre-paid pump. Mesophyll PEPcase loads carbon dioxide into a four-carbon acid. The bundle sheath unloads it as a concentrated burst for RuBisCO. Load, ship, unload — and every C four question is somewhere on that one line.

The second pro-tip is for limiting factors. Picture a thali assembly line moving at the speed of whichever dish is in shortest supply. Raising any other ingredient will not speed things up until you fix the slow one. That image answers every plateau question and every greenhouse scenario the paper can build.

Test it on the classic scenario. A C three crop in a sealed, brightly lit greenhouse stops gaining biomass by afternoon despite ample light and water. Which factor is limiting? Light is plentiful and water is plentiful — so neither can be the slow dish. In a sealed space, photosynthesis has depleted the available carbon dioxide, and carbon dioxide is now the bottleneck.

<whisper>And four mnemonics for the last minute. 'P E P loads, RuBisCO reaps'. 'Four equals O A A, three equals P G A'. 'Photorespiration: oxygen in, carbon dioxide out, nothing gained'. And 'the slowest dish sets the thali speed'.
ये subtopic chapter के सबसे ज़्यादा पूछे जाने वाले हिस्सों में है, और चार pitfalls लगभग हर कटे mark की वजह हैं। फिर दो तस्वीरें — एक pump और एक thali line — पूरा subtopic exam hall तक ले जाती हैं।

Pitfall one: C three और C four के नंबर आपस में मिला देना। इन्हें जोड़ियों में fix करो। C three: acceptor R u B P, पाँच carbon; product three P G A, तीन carbon। C four: acceptor P E P, तीन carbon; product O A A, चार carbon। और वो rule जो confusion रोकता है: नाम first product के carbon count से आता है, acceptor के नहीं।

Pitfall two: photorespiration को 'respiration in light' कहना। ये आम respiration नहीं है। आम respiration A T P बनाती है; photorespiration ज़रा भी नहीं। ये RuBisCO की oxygenase वाली भूल है, और ये plant को carbon कमाकर नहीं देती, उसका carbon ख़र्च करा देती है।

Pitfall three: भूल जाना कि C four में कौन-सा enzyme और कौन-सी cell क्या करती है। PEPcase, mesophyll, पहली capture। RuBisCO, bundle sheath, Calvin cycle। इन्हें उलटना classic ग़लती है, और paper तुम्हें वो उलटा हुआ version option की तरह ज़रूर देगा।

Pitfall four ज़्यादा सूक्ष्म है और अच्छे students को पकड़ता है: ये सोचना कि C four plants Calvin cycle इस्तेमाल नहीं करते। बिलकुल करते हैं। RuBisCO और Calvin cycle चलते हैं — बस bundle sheath के अंदर, ऊँची carbon dioxide पर, महफ़ूज़ तरीक़े से। C four, Calvin का विकल्प नहीं है; वो Calvin के लिए delivery service है।

अब पहला pro-tip। C four को carbon dioxide का pre-paid pump समझो। Mesophyll का PEPcase carbon dioxide को चार-carbon वाले acid में load करता है। Bundle sheath उसे RuBisCO के लिए गाढ़े burst की तरह unload करता है। Load, ship, unload — और हर C four सवाल इसी एक line पर कहीं न कहीं बैठा है।

दूसरा pro-tip limiting factors के लिए है। एक thali line सोचो जो उसी रफ़्तार से चलती है जिस dish की सबसे कम supply हो। कोई भी दूसरा ingredient बढ़ाने से रफ़्तार नहीं बढ़ेगी, जब तक सुस्त वाली ठीक न हो। यही तस्वीर हर plateau सवाल और हर greenhouse scenario का जवाब दे देती है।

Classic scenario पर आज़माओ। एक बंद, तेज़ रोशनी वाले greenhouse में C three crop दोपहर तक biomass बढ़ाना बंद कर देता है, जबकि light और water भरपूर हैं। कौन-सा factor limiting है? Light भरपूर, water भरपूर — तो ये दोनों सुस्त dish नहीं हो सकते। बंद जगह में photosynthesis ने मौजूद carbon dioxide चट कर दी है, और अब carbon dioxide ही bottleneck है।

<whisper>और आख़िरी मिनट के लिए चार mnemonics। 'P E P loads, RuBisCO reaps'। 'चार बराबर O A A, तीन बराबर P G A'। 'Photorespiration: oxygen in, carbon dioxide out, nothing gained'। और 'सबसे सुस्त dish thali की रफ़्तार तय करती है'।

sections.title: Chapter cheat sheet: the whole of photosynthesis on one board

board_events.text: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants — quick recall
Overall equation: $6\,CO_2 + 12\,H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6\,O_2 + 6\,H_2O$ — the O2 comes from WATER.

Scientists: Priestley (restored air) · Ingenhousz (light + green parts) · Sachs (glucose stored as starch) · Engelmann (first action spectrum: Cladophora + prism + bacteria) · van Niel (O2 from water).

Pigments: chl a (blue-green, CHIEF) · chl b (yellow-green) · xanthophylls (yellow) · carotenoids (yellow-orange). Accessory pigments widen range, funnel energy, protect chl a. Absorption and action spectra both peak in blue and red; green is least effective.

Light reaction (thylakoid membrane / grana): PS II = P680, splits water, releases O2. PS I = P700, makes NADPH. Route: water → PS II → PS I → NADP+. Non-cyclic = both PS, O2 + ATP + NADPH; cyclic = PS I only, ATP alone (Arnon).

Chemiosmosis: H+ piled into the lumen (water-splitting + carrier pumping + NADP+ reduction) → back out through ATP synthase (F0 channel + F1 head in the stroma) → ATP. The gradient is the real energy store — it works even in the dark.

Calvin cycle (C3, in the stroma): acceptor RuBP (5C) · enzyme RuBisCO · first stable product 3-PGA (3C) · reduced product PGAL. Phases: Carboxylation → Reduction → Regeneration. Per glucose: 6 CO2 + 18 ATP + 12 NADPH (6 turns); per turn 3 ATP + 2 NADPH.

C4 (Hatch-Slack): acceptor PEP · enzyme PEPcase (mesophyll) · first product OAA (4C) → malate → bundle sheath → decarboxylation → CO2 burst → Calvin cycle (RuBisCO). Kranz anatomy present. Maize, sugarcane, sorghum.

Photorespiration: RuBisCO oxygenase at low CO2/O2 → 2C glycolate → chloroplast + peroxisome + mitochondrion → releases CO2, makes no sugar/ATP/NADPH. Present in C3, absent in C4. Blackman: the rate is set by the factor nearest its minimum.

Mnemonics: 'Pigs In Sachs's Engine, Never CO2' · 'Water → II → I → NADP' · 'Two-Eighty splits, Seven-Hundred ships' · 'Lumen Loads, Stroma Spends' · 'Catch, Cook, Rebuild' · '18 before 12' · 'PEP loads, RuBisCO reaps'.

segments.text: One board, the whole chapter. This is a recall section, not a teaching one — everything here you have already built, so let it come back fast rather than slow.

The overall equation: six carbon dioxide plus twelve water gives glucose, six oxygen, six water. Twelve in, six out — and the oxygen comes from water. That is the chapter's most-tested fact, sitting in its first equation.

The scientists, in order. Priestley restored spoiled air. Ingenhousz added light and green parts. Sachs found glucose stored as starch. Engelmann gave the first action spectrum with Cladophora, a prism and bacteria. van Niel showed the oxygen comes from water.

The pigments. Chlorophyll a, blue-green, the chief. Chlorophyll b, yellow-green. Xanthophylls, yellow. Carotenoids, yellow-orange. Accessory pigments widen the range, funnel energy to chlorophyll a, and protect it. And both spectra — absorption and action — peak in blue and red; green is least effective, which is why leaves look green.

The light reaction, on the thylakoid membranes of the grana. Photosystem two is P six eighty: it splits water and releases oxygen. Photosystem one is P seven hundred: it makes N A D P H. Route: water, to two, to one, to N A D P plus. Non-cyclic uses both photosystems and yields oxygen, A T P and N A D P H. Cyclic uses Photosystem one alone and yields A T P only. Both terms are Arnon's.

Chemiosmosis. Protons piled into the lumen by three sources — water-splitting, carrier pumping, and N A D P reduction — then back out through A T P synthase, F zero channel and F one head in the stroma, making A T P. The gradient is the real energy store, which is why acidified thylakoids make A T P in total darkness.

The Calvin cycle, in the stroma. Acceptor R u B P, five carbons. Enzyme RuBisCO. First stable product three P G A, three carbons. Reduced product P G A L. Phases: carboxylation, reduction, regeneration. Per glucose: six carbon dioxide, eighteen A T P, twelve N A D P H, across six turns. Per turn: three A T P and two N A D P H.

The C four pathway. Acceptor P E P, enzyme PEPcase in the mesophyll, first product O A A with four carbons. It becomes malate, ships to the bundle sheath, gets decarboxylated into a carbon dioxide burst, and feeds an ordinary Calvin cycle under RuBisCO. Kranz anatomy present. Maize, sugarcane, sorghum.

And the last two. Photorespiration: RuBisCO as oxygenase when the carbon-dioxide-to-oxygen ratio is low, running through two-carbon glycolate across chloroplast, peroxisome and mitochondrion, releasing carbon dioxide and making no sugar, no A T P, no N A D P H. Present in C three, absent in C four. And Blackman: the rate is set by the factor nearest its minimum value.

<whisper>Finally, the seven mnemonics, all in one place. 'Pigs In Sachs's Engine, Never C O two'. 'Water to two to one to N A D P'. 'Two-Eighty splits, Seven-Hundred ships'. 'Lumen Loads, Stroma Spends'. 'Catch, Cook, Rebuild'. 'Eighteen before twelve'. And 'P E P loads, RuBisCO reaps'.
एक board, पूरा chapter। ये recall section है, teaching नहीं — यहाँ का सब कुछ तुम पहले ही बना चुके हो, तो इसे धीरे नहीं, तेज़ी से वापस आने दो।

Overall equation: छह carbon dioxide plus बारह water देते हैं glucose, छह oxygen, छह water। बारह अंदर, छह बाहर — और oxygen water से आती है। Chapter का सबसे ज़्यादा पूछा जाने वाला fact, उसकी पहली ही equation में बैठा हुआ।

Scientists, क्रम में। Priestley ने spoiled air restore की। Ingenhousz ने light और green parts जोड़े। Sachs ने glucose को starch की तरह stored पाया। Engelmann ने Cladophora, prism और bacteria से पहला action spectrum दिया। van Niel ने दिखाया कि oxygen water से आती है।

Pigments। Chlorophyll a, blue-green, chief। Chlorophyll b, yellow-green। Xanthophylls, yellow। Carotenoids, yellow-orange। Accessory pigments range चौड़ी करते हैं, energy chlorophyll a तक funnel करते हैं, और उसे बचाते हैं। और दोनों spectra — absorption और action — blue और red में peak करते हैं; green सबसे कम effective, इसीलिए leaves हरी दिखती हैं।

Light reaction, grana की thylakoid membranes पर। Photosystem two यानी P six eighty: water तोड़ता है, oxygen छोड़ता है। Photosystem one यानी P seven hundred: N A D P H बनाता है। Route: water, फिर two, फिर one, फिर N A D P plus। Non-cyclic दोनों photosystems इस्तेमाल करता है और oxygen, A T P तथा N A D P H देता है। Cyclic अकेला Photosystem one चलाता है और सिर्फ़ A T P देता है। दोनों terms Arnon के हैं।

Chemiosmosis। तीन sources से lumen में protons की ढेरी — water-splitting, carrier pumping, और N A D P reduction — फिर A T P synthase से वापसी, F zero channel और stroma में F one head, और A T P तैयार। असली energy store gradient है, इसीलिए acidified thylakoids पूरे अँधेरे में भी A T P बनाते हैं।

Calvin cycle, stroma में। Acceptor R u B P, पाँच carbon। Enzyme RuBisCO। First stable product three P G A, तीन carbon। Reduced product P G A L। Phases: carboxylation, reduction, regeneration। हर glucose पर: छह carbon dioxide, अठारह A T P, बारह N A D P H, छह turns में। हर turn पर: तीन A T P और दो N A D P H।

C four pathway। Acceptor P E P, enzyme PEPcase mesophyll में, first product O A A चार carbon के साथ। वो malate बनता है, bundle sheath जाता है, decarboxylate होकर carbon dioxide का burst देता है, और RuBisCO के नीचे आम Calvin cycle को खिलाता है। Kranz anatomy मौजूद। Maize, sugarcane, sorghum।

और आख़िरी दो। Photorespiration: कम carbon dioxide-से-oxygen ratio पर RuBisCO oxygenase बनकर, दो-carbon वाले glycolate के रास्ते chloroplast, peroxisome और mitochondrion में चलकर, carbon dioxide छोड़ता है और न sugar देता है, न A T P, न N A D P H। C three में मौजूद, C four में ग़ैरहाज़िर। और Blackman: rate वही factor तय करता है जो अपनी न्यूनतम क़ीमत के सबसे क़रीब है।

<whisper>आख़िर में, सातों mnemonics, एक ही जगह। 'Pigs In Sachs's Engine, Never C O two'। 'Water to two to one to N A D P'। 'Two-Eighty splits, Seven-Hundred ships'। 'Lumen Loads, Stroma Spends'। 'Catch, Cook, Rebuild'। 'Eighteen before twelve'। और 'P E P loads, RuBisCO reaps'।
